commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Functions whose retail code has the same instructions as a matched
rac2-decomp (Going Commando) function, apart from addresses, take that
C with its names renamed to this game's: every relocated name is read
from the compiled object against rac3's retail bytes. Small-data
choices are spelled as section attributes where rac2's file used a
different -G. Each carries a one-line note naming its rac2 source;
those from MIT-licensed rac2 files keep that file's notice.

commits.headline: feat(tools): build switch jump tables in level C from the compiler's .rodata
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Level C could not have a switch: gcc writes the jump table into the file's
.rodata, but a level is linked from one text.c.o whose .rodata the linker
script discards, and level_symbols.py refused any object with data. In retail
the tables sit in each level's .data, in one block of the source files'
read-only data whose order is not .text's and whose place differs per level.

level_symbols.py now takes a file's .rodata from where its %hi/%lo read it and
checks every word there against the level…

commits.headline: fix(tools): build the linker's 0xCD fill after a level's C function
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A source file whose code ends on a 4-mod-8 address is followed in retail by one
0xCDCDCDCD word where the next file's .align 3 starts, and the catalogue size of
its last function includes it. The level C build padded with zeros there
(func_L39_00515FE0). level_tree.py now puts TEXT_FILL(N), a new macro in
include_asm.h, after a C function whose catalogue size ends in fill words.

commits.headline: fix(tools): link a core C object's literal pools where retail has them
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A double or float constant gcc cannot make an immediate goes into the object's
.rodata, and boot_elf's linker script discarded it: the relocations resolved to 0,
so the full build differed (func_00120730, an @ee29 function) though the
per-function check matched. tools/core_rodata.py finds the section's bytes once
in the retail program, cuts the core blob around them (split_data) and links the
object's .rodata between the halves, in a derived build/<target>/<target>.ld that
build.py uses.

commits.headline: fix(tools): split a level's data around a jump table that ends 4 mod 8
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A table of an odd number of words (a 5-case switch) ends 4 mod 8, and the data
after it is a piece whose header carries the file's .align 3: the piece cannot
start there, and split_data() refused the level (func_L20_003F4520,
func_L39_004EB840 and others). The words up to the first 8-aligned item now get
a piece of their own, a 4-aligned .text piece, so everything keeps its address.
